138.0.0.en: I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.

138.0.1.en: 1- David thanks God not only with his tongue but with all his feelings, that is, from his heart, and praises Him at all times, even in the midst of troubles, especially since God accepted him in spite of his sins and weakness and brought him into His presence, so that he stood before Him giving thanks. This also means that there is nothing in David's heart but God, since he praises Him with his whole heart. He had already lived out the words of Christ, who declared, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart" (Mt 22:37).

138.0.2.en: 2- David sings with joy before the gods, that is, the angels, as the Septuagint translation mentions. David rose above earthly things to heavenly things and stood before God, who is surrounded by the angels, who give thanks to God and praise Him continually. Among the angels he imitates them, leaves aside earthly concerns, and occupies himself with heaven and its spirituality. When he feels that he is among the angels, he not only rises up to them, but they also condescend and share the praise with him. For this reason the Church is called the house of the angels, and many angels and saints have appeared and shared the praise with those on earth, in many apparitions. He also sings before the gods, that is, the kings, the rulers of the world. He bears witness to God boldly everywhere, even before the great ones of the world.

138.0.3.en: 3- By the gods may be meant the pagans and their gods. David boldly gives thanks to God before the pagan nations with their gods, which are not gods but mere idols. He praises the true God, who is God, and gives Him thanks with all his heart.

138.1.0.en: I will worship toward thy holy temple, and praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth: for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.

138.1.1.en: 1- David praises God for His mercy, because He accepted him and forgave him his many sins, and he also thanks Him for His truth, because God showed the truth by rescuing him from the hand of Saul and Absalom, rescuing him also from the hand of his enemies and giving him victory over them. He declares his thanks and his submission to God by worshipping in His holy temple, meaning the tabernacle of meeting before the ark of the covenant, especially after David fell into his great sins, repented of them, was forgiven by God, and was permitted by Him to worship before His temple.

138.1.2.en: 2- David's thanks to God for His mercy and truth is a type of our thanks for His redemption of us on the Cross, in which mercy and truth met: mercy in taking away our sins, and truth in satisfying divine justice through the death of Christ on our behalf.

138.1.3.en: 3- God magnified His word above all His name. The name of God means His person; that is, the God known in the Old Testament to His people declared Himself with a great declaration in His commandments and His law, which He gave to Moses, and then His greatness increased as He declared Himself in His Incarnation and redemption. Although God was hidden and humbled in the form of human flesh, it is the greatest declaration that we see God walking among us in perfection as an example for us, then taking up our sins on the Cross, and after this rising from the dead by the power of His divinity. By this Christ was exalted above every name in heaven and on earth when He declared His divinity by His Resurrection (Phil 2:9).

138.2.0.en: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.

138.2.1.en: 1- David declares his daily experience with God, that He answers his requests. This of course gladdens him and reassures him. And not only this, but God encourages him with a divine power within him, so that he may move, bear all responsibilities and succeed, and God also guides him in all his circumstances, whether to rise up and fight or to withdraw and flee.

138.2.2.en: 2- God's answer to David is a type of His answer to the human race by His Incarnation in the fullness of time and by His giving of the Holy Spirit as a permanent gift dwelling in the new man, giving him strength for life with God and for service, however great his weakness, as happened with the Apostles, to whom He gave strength to endure and courage to face every situation and to preach everywhere (Acts 5:41).

138.2.3.en: How beautiful it is to feel heaven while you pray, and the presence of God and His angels who praise Him, so that you rise above every sin by repentance, cast off the cares of the world, and your heart is drawn to the person of God, so that you praise Him and enjoy being in His hands.

138.3.s.en: (2) The Most High, who loves the humble

138.3.0.en: All the kings of the earth shall praise thee, O LORD, when they hear the words of thy mouth.

138.3.1.en: 1- When the kings of the earth praise God, this means that they have heard His word and believed in Him; this is a prophecy of the entry of the Gentiles into the faith. The kings of the earth are the kings of the pagan nations, and this is a prophecy of the spread of Christianity throughout the whole earth.

138.3.2.en: 2- The kings of the earth are all the spiritual believers who have controlled themselves against the lusts of the earth, and God reigns over their hearts; they have heard His commandments, kept them and lived by them, and so they were then able to praise Him.

138.4.0.en: Yea, they shall sing in the ways of the LORD: for great is the glory of the LORD.

138.4.1.en: Those who praise will sing in the ways of the Lord, that is, His commandments, because they have kept them, and they have worked in their hearts and appeared in beautiful praises to God. They have even felt the greatness and glory of God and so humbled themselves before Him, whatever their position; and the more they repent, the more their humility grows and their praise rises.

138.5.0.en: Though the LORD be high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly: but the proud he knoweth afar off.

138.5.1.en: 1- Despite the perfection of God's virtues, and although He is higher than all men and angels, His heart is full of love, so He is tender toward the humble, while the proud He keeps far from Him, for they do not love God but themselves. The humble person feels his need of God and loves Him, so God pours out His mercies and blessings upon him. The proud person, however, deprives himself of God's gifts.

138.5.2.en: 2- The humble one is David, who loves God and feels His loftiness, so God sees him, condescends to him and embraces him with His blessings. But David's proud enemies, such as Saul and his servants, God keeps far from Him because of their pride.

138.5.3.en: Humility is the shortest way to the heart of God; by it you obtain all your requests, and His mercies are poured out upon you beyond what you ask or think. Be sure that your sins do not hinder you from enjoying God as long as you repent of them. God loves the weak, supports them and has compassion on them, and for this reason He blessed them, saying, "Blessed are the poor in spirit." [3] The one who delivers from troubles (vv. 7, 8):

138.6.0.en: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.

138.6.1.en: 1- One who believes in God and praises Him is not disturbed by troubles, for God is able to give him a peaceful and happy life despite the troubles around him. It is not necessary that God remove the trouble, but He gives His children a life full of joy in the midst of troubles (Jn 16:33).

138.6.2.en: 2- If the enemies rise up in anger to harm me, they cannot, because Your right hand, O Lord, saves me from their plots and their evil, as God saved David from the hands of Saul and Absalom.

138.6.3.en: 3- The right hand of God is a type of the incarnate Christ, who saved us from the wrath of the devil, who accuses us and wants to destroy us, and by His Cross He not only saves us but gives us life, even in the midst of troubles.

138.6.4.en: Our life on earth is the trouble from which we are delivered, if we live heavenly lives on earth.

138.6.5.en: 4- One who lives with his eyes toward heaven is not distressed by the troubles of the earth, for he sees the vastness of God's love and lives heavenly by the Spirit, so that he rejoices at all times while he is on earth, the earth of troubles.

138.7.0.en: The LORD will plead for me: thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.

138.7.1.en: 1- David concludes the psalm by declaring his faith and the secret of his peace of mind, which is God's protection of him, who repels from him all the attacks of enemies and protects him if he walks in the midst of them.

138.7.2.en: 2- David also trusts that God's mercy is what keeps him throughout his life, for He forgives his sins and pours out His blessings upon him. This mercy continues with him on the day of judgment, so that God does not condemn him, because of his faith and repentance, and God's mercy toward him grows greater in the blessings of eternity.

138.7.3.en: 3- David's peace is built on his trust in God, who protects him and continues in His protection of him. Even if men forsake him and become enemies as well, God cannot forsake him, even if the whole world stands against him, for God is with him, as happened with St. Athanasius the Apostolic.

138.7.4.en: How beautiful is peace of mind in the hands of God! Rely on Him and accept His will in your life, even if it seems difficult, because He is able to bring you through in peace in the midst of sufferings and to make your heart rejoice at all times.

138.7.5.en: The Psalm The Psalm The One Hundred and Thirty-Ninth The Eighty-Ninth God's perfect knowledge For the choir director. Of David. A psalm: "O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me" (v. 1). Introduction

138.7.6.en: 1- Its author: the prophet David, as the title of this psalm states.

138.7.7.en: 2- Many commentators consider this psalm the crown of the psalms, because it declares David's practical spiritual experience of God and speaks about it in detail throughout the psalm.

138.7.8.en: 3- This psalm suits the one who prays, who loves God, wants to live in His embrace, and rejects evil.

138.7.9.en: 4- The psalm calls us to examine ourselves and review ourselves in the light of God's word and commandments (v. 23).

138.7.10.en: 5- This psalm speaks in detail about the attributes of God, His knowledge of hidden things, His presence everywhere, and His authority over everything.

138.7.11.en: 6- The psalmist rebukes the wicked and calls them to repent quickly, because persisting in evil will inevitably lead them to destruction (vv. 19, 20).

138.7.12.en: 7- There is a similarity between this psalm and the Book of Job (Job 10).

138.7.13.en: 8- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.

139.0.s.en: (1) The One who knows all and is present everywhere

139.0.0.en: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me. Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off. Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways. For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, thou knowest it altogether.

139.0.2.en: Lying down (marbad): the place where animals rest, and what is meant is my place of rest.

139.0.3.en: 1- David declares to God, as he speaks with Him in private conversation: You, O God, know everything about me by complete examination and scrutiny, like one who winnows grain to separate it from the chaff. You know the good and the evil that is in me and in all my inclinations, and not only my deeds and my words; You know my character; You know me in my rest and in my distress, and You even know what I intend to do or say. You see from afar all that is in me, and You do not need to associate with me as men do in order to know me, because You are my Creator, and You have complete knowledge of all that is in me.

139.0.4.en: 2- These verses are a type of the voice of Christ in the flesh in His converse with the Father, and since the two are of one essence, the Father knows all that is in the Son and knows His love for mankind, how He humbled Himself in His Incarnation, and how He would suffer and bear all the evil of humanity on His shoulders when He is crucified and dies for the sake of redemption.

139.1.0.en: Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me.

139.1.1.en: You know everything about me, O Lord: what has passed in my life, recently or long ago, and what will happen in the future. You also know where I go, what I will succeed in or fail at, what I will grow in spiritually and what I am unable to do. Your hand is upon me, protecting me and keeping evil away from me as long as I seek You. You are the Controller of all; to You I flee for refuge, and I trust in Your hand that protects me. And if I think of evil, You declare to me Your fear so that I repent. I rest and am at peace in Your hand; even if You allow troubles to come upon me, they are for my benefit and to protect me from many evils.

139.2.0.en: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it.

139.2.1.en: You, O Lord, know everything about me, while I can know only a little about You, because You are unlimited and I am limited. You are wonderful; I cannot contain You, but You contain me, and You make Yourself known to me as much as I can bear, and Your knowledge of everything about me is beyond my understanding and is wonderful in my eyes.

139.3.0.en: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there. If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea; even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.

139.3.1.en: 1- David shows that he cannot flee from God, even if he turns in any direction in the world, for God is present and sees him and is able to take hold of him and do two things with him:

139.3.2.en: a - He guides him and brings him back to Himself and to the spiritual life with Him, however much he has been occupied with other things or has gone far away on a wrong path. This shows God's love, which gladdens the heart of man.

139.3.3.en: b - He restrains him by His justice and judges him, and this produces the fear of God within the heart, so that it makes him keep away from evil and remember always that God is before him.

139.3.4.en: 2- God appears in His Holy Trinity in (v. 7): "Thy spirit," that is, the Holy Spirit, and "thy presence," that is, the incarnate Son, while the Father is the One whom David addresses.

139.3.5.en: 3- The vertical direction appears in (v. 8) in ascending to heaven, the place of the righteous, or making one's bed in Hades, that is, lying in the grave and in death. This is what David imagined: by rising up to heaven, or going down below, he would find God, who is everywhere, to glorify the righteous in heaven and to judge the wicked in Hades. On the other hand, if he goes horizontally with the beginning of the morning, to reach the uttermost parts of the earth, God is present everywhere. The vertical direction and the horizontal direction are a type of the Cross on which Christ was crucified to save all, everyone who believes in Him in every one of the four directions, for He is the Savior of all humanity.

139.4.0.en: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.

139.4.1.en: Shall cover me (taghshani): shall envelop me.

139.4.2.en: 1- A man may feel that he is in darkness where no one sees him, so that he may do evil in the darkness of the night, but he forgets that God is light and lights up the night with His light; it is He who created the sun to give light to the day, and the moon and stars to give light to the night, and He is the searcher of hearts and reins. So even if the wicked man hides himself in the darkness of the night, God sees all his deeds, his thoughts and the feelings of his heart.

139.4.3.en: 2- If the children of God walk in the darkness of the night, let them not fear evil, because God lights up their lives and keeps them from their enemies the demons and from every temptation. If sins attack them to darken their thoughts, God warns them by His light so that they reject all evil, and if they fall into the darkness of sin, God pricks them by His Holy Spirit so that they hasten to repentance.

139.4.4.en: 3- "The night shineth as the day." If darkness is the nature of the night, and at the same time God's nature is light and brightness, so also the dark temptation appears harsh and difficult to a person.

139.4.5.en: But with God it is bright, and for the benefit and good of the person, and He makes it bright and comforting to him, that is, He turns feelings of distress into rest and peace, and even joy.

139.4.6.en: 4- "The night shineth as the day" is a prophecy of the Resurrection of Christ, the true Light, who rose from the darkness of the tomb in the light of His great glory.

139.4.7.en: 5- "The night is light about me" means the turning of elements into the opposite of their nature: the night is dark and the day is bright, but the night shines, just as God made the fire gentle for the three young men although it burned the Babylonians who threw the three young men into the fire (Dan 3:27).

139.5.0.en: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother's womb. I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

139.5.1.en: 1- God possessed my reins, that is, He possessed my feelings, because above the kidney lies the adrenal gland, which is responsible for a person's emotions. What is meant is that God possessed me wholly, with all my abilities and affections, and it is He who made me, as a craftsman makes a woven fabric, and formed me gradually in my mother's womb. By this, God is the One who knows everything about me, and He contains me and leads me in the way of righteousness if I walk with Him.

139.5.2.en: 2- The making of man is distinguished from the rest of creation in his body and spirit. This calls for thanksgiving and glorifying of God, and indeed every person is distinguished from other human beings, which shows God's special love for every person. This gives a person confidence and strength because of God's care for him personally.

139.5.3.en: 3- The works of God the Creator in me and in the rest of creatures are beyond my mind, but by faith my soul understands this wonder that God has made. And as knowledge advances, it discovers something of God's wonderful works in the creation of man and of the rest of creatures.

139.6.0.en: My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret, and curiously wrought in the lowest parts of the earth. Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

139.6.1.en: 1- God formed in His mind an image of man; that is, in secret man was in the thought of God, and this from eternity. At the proper time He created him with precision, so that each bone of man, however small, had a number with God, that is, it was known and counted. And because God created man from dust, he says, "curiously wrought in the lowest parts of the earth." God formed the members of man, which were in God's book, that is, written in His mind, and He even knows their past, present and future. So everything is known to God from eternity, and all that will happen to him. All this shows God's love and care, which surpass the mind; there is no one who cares like Him, not even man cares for himself as God cares for him.

139.6.2.en: 2- God sees man with his shortcomings and rejoices in him as he grows and matures, and this gives hope to every person who is weak and lacking in understanding and maturity, for God loves him, accepts him and makes him grow until he is perfected.

139.7.0.en: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them! If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand: when I awake, I am still with thee.

139.7.1.en: 1- The thoughts of God, His plans and His love for His creation are so many that they cannot be counted, because God is unlimited, and His love and care for man are unlimited; how great is the sum of them, and they are more than the sand. This makes a person thank God at all times, and it is not possible to comprehend the preciousness and greatness of God's thoughts, but a person believes in God's infinite love for him.

139.7.2.en: 2- God loves man before he is born, so when a person awakes, that is, is born, he finds God with him, caring for him. And if a person sleeps every day and awakes, he finds God's care surrounding him in his sleep and in his waking.

139.7.3.en: And if a person neglects himself or his spiritual life, then is roused by the action of the Holy Spirit of God, he finds God's love with him always.

139.7.4.en: Look at God's love and care for you from the time you were born until now, so that your heart may be at peace, and you may thank Him, trust in your soul that relies on God, go forth in works of love for God and people, and gladden God at all times.

139.8.0.en: Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God: depart from me therefore, ye bloody men. For they speak against thee wickedly, and thine enemies take thy name in vain. Do not I hate them, O LORD, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee? I hate them with perfect hatred:

139.8.3.en: Since David loved God, he also loved the good and lived in it, and consequently could no longer bear evil, and was distressed by the wicked because of their evils. Although he wishes for their repentance and salvation, why does David hate them?

139.8.4.en: 1- He hates their evil because it is against God, and they are God's enemies.

139.8.5.en: 2- Because the wicked are deceivers who pretend to piety but cling to evil, so they deceive themselves and may deceive others.

139.8.6.en: 3- David fears that he may be affected by their evil, even partially, and stumble and fall into one of the evils they do.

139.8.7.en: 4- David was moved and utterly hated the wicked's contempt for the lives of the righteous and their killing of them.

139.8.8.en: 5- David was also distressed by the wicked's abuse and their killing of others morally, that is, they directed to them hard words that a person cannot bear, so David was moved because of the humiliation of the righteous.

139.9.0.en: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: and see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

139.9.1.en: After David showed his rejection of evil, he draws near to God with humility, asking God to search him and to test his thoughts, lest there be any evil within him, or any negligence however small, so that God may cleanse him from it. The wicked way is anything that has no benefit and does not bring a person nearer to God, but on the contrary, with time, a person may fall into great evils. This shows David's carefulness and his concern for his purity, and also his concern for his eternal life, for he does not want to be hindered by any evil, and so we are assured that he did not reject evil out of pride, but out of aversion to evil and love for righteousness. He loves the wicked and hates their evil, which he mentioned in (v. 21), and this hatred is not considered a wicked way but is the love of God and purity of heart toward the wicked, for he wishes for their repentance.

139.9.2.en: Be careful in your relationships, and in the places where you sit, so that you keep away from sources of evil; this will help you toward a life of righteousness and a growing relationship of love with God.

139.9.3.en: God who delivers from evil For the choir director. Of David. A psalm: "Deliver me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man" (v. 1). Introduction:

139.9.4.en: 1- Its author: the prophet David, as the title of the psalm states.

139.9.5.en: 2- When was it written? When David was driven from the presence of King Saul.

139.9.6.en: 3- This psalm suits everyone who suffers from the wicked and asks for God's deliverance.

139.9.7.en: 4- There is a similarity between this psalm and the three psalms that follow it, all of which show the suffering of the righteous man and his request for deliverance from God, and it is also similar to Psalms 58 and 64.

139.9.8.en: 5- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
